summary: @dreamguyxeon/libsignal-node hijacks sibling @whiskeysockets/baileys and remote-controls installer's WhatsApp session
details: Package publishes as @dreamguyxeon/libsignal-node with a README presenting it as the legitimate libsignal-node Signal-protocol library, but the shipped code is unrelated to libsignal. On require() of index.js, install.js locates the installer's @whiskeysockets/baileys under node_modules and overwrites lib/Socket/newsletter.js with an embedded replacement. The injected newsletter.js sets a timer to fetch https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DGXeon13/strings/refs/heads/main/strings.json and iterates the returned channel IDs, issuing WhatsApp newsletter FOLLOW queries through the host application's authenticated Baileys socket. After patching, install.js calls process.exit(0) after 20 seconds to force the host bot to restart and load the modified module. The attacker retains ongoing control over the driven actions via the mutable main branch of the attacker-owned DGXeon13/strings repository, and the injection point (overwriting a sibling package's source file) can be repurposed beyond follow operations.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
